keywords.def: Random Access Memory: temporary, volatile main memory; data is lost when power is off.
Read Only Memory: permanent, non-volatile memory with start-up instructions built in at the factory.
Memory that loses its data when the power is turned off.

en.text: Storage devices keep files. They are primary or secondary. Primary storage is the main memory. RAM holds the programs and data the CPU is using; it is read-write and volatile, so its data is lost when the power goes off. ROM is permanent and non-volatile, built in at the factory, and holds the start-up instructions. CMOS keeps some information when the computer is shut off.

screens.title: Power cut!
screens.ask: The power goes off while you are typing and you had not saved. Why is your work lost?
opts: It was only in RAM, which is volatile
screens.after: Unsaved work lives in RAM, which loses its data when the power is turned off.
